image_description: A large, white modular bookcase system spanning the width of the image. It consists of multiple vertical bays (approximately 5-6 visible sections) with adjustable shelving. The shelves contain a sparse arrangement of books and decorative objects (a red vase, a yellow folder). The structure appears to be made of painted wood or MDF. The perspective is slightly angled from the left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Rectangular furniture piece of considerable height, notably taller than wide.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The overall unit is significantly wider than it is tall (landscape orientation), contradicting the 'notably taller than wide' description typical of a single standalone bookcase, though individual bays are taller than wide.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tall rectangular frame with horizontal divisions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The structure clearly exhibits a rectangular grid pattern with distinct horizontal shelves dividing the vertical space.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bilateral symmetry with open front displaying books and objects.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the individual modules are symmetrical, the entire assembly lacks bilateral symmetry due to the asymmetrical placement of objects and the cropping of the unit on the right side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Multiple horizontal shelves spaced evenly from top to bottom.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Each vertical bay contains multiple shelves that appear evenly spaced vertically.
Adjustability is an internal mechanical feature not visually verifiable without seeing pin holes or brackets clearly; current resolution/angle makes this ambiguous.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some models have glass doors on upper section.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No glass doors are visible on any part of the bookcase; all shelves are open.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Constructed from wood particleboard or metal with finished surface stained painted or laminated.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface has a smooth, uniform white finish consistent with painted wood or laminate/MDF.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Front open displaying books and objects on each shelf.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front is entirely open, and various objects (books, vases) are placed on the shelves.
There is no visible decorative hardware (handles, knobs); the design is minimalist.

artifact_observations.location: Right edge of the bookcase and floor line
artifact_observations.reasoning: The vertical lines on the far right seem to warp slightly inward, and the connection between the bookcase base and the floor lacks a sharp, physically accurate shadow line, suggesting slight geometric instability.
The spines of the books lack distinct text or logical separation; they appear as fused blocks of color with 'melting' edges rather than distinct physical objects.

artifact_observations.location: Top-right corner of the central red object
artifact_observations.reasoning: The red decorative object has an ill-defined geometry where the handle/top merges ambiguously with the body, lacking clear structural logic.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the primary classification and distinguish between a single unit vs. modular wall system.
To verify if the shelves have consistent depth and if the back panel exists as a continuous plane without warping.
To check for fusion artifacts between objects and shelves, and ensure objects are topologically distinct.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of vertical dividers (are they straight?)
Consistency of shelf depth across all bays
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'books' on the shelves. AI often fails to render them as distinct rectangular prisms, resulting in melted shapes. Also, verify if the vertical dividers align perfectly with the floor; misalignment here is a common geometric artifact in architectural AI generations.
